label: prf:bar-parity-split
title: Proof of the bar-parity split
html:
Proof. Proof of the bar-parity split

Let \sigma be the bar-involution (def:bar-involution), a linear map with \sigma^2 = \mathrm{id}. For any x,

\mathrm{even}(x) + \mathrm{odd}(x) = (x + \sigma x) + (x - \sigma x) = 2x,

thus the two parities sum to 2x (evenPart_add_oddPart); when 2 is invertible in the coefficient ring (characteristic \neq 2), x is half their sum — but the decomposition itself needs no division. The even part is \sigma-fixed: \sigma(x + \sigma x) = \sigma x + \sigma^2 x = \sigma x + x = x + \sigma x (evenPart_fixed, using \sigma^2=\mathrm{id} and additivity). The odd part is \sigma-anti: \sigma(x - \sigma x) = \sigma x - x = -(x - \sigma x) (oddPart_anti). Hence the bar-even subspace (\cosh, (q+q^{-1})/2) and the bar-odd subspace (\sinh, (q-q^{-1})/2) are complementary, and any fibre element decomposes uniquely across them. The binding trace \tau lives in the even subspace and the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta residue in the odd subspace, so both are determined by the single element they jointly span. \qquad\blacksquare
